chunks: Ḥumrān ibn Aʿyan asked him about a man who says:
"Release me where You have restrained me."
He said: "He is released where Allah, the Mighty and Majestic, has restrained him, whether he said it or did not say it."

key_terms.اللَّهُ: Allah, the One determining the impediment
key_terms.حُلَّنِي: Release me from the state of iḥrām or its restriction
key_terms.حِلٌّ: Released from restriction; lawful exit from the state

ai.seo_question: If a muḥrim is prevented from continuing, does saying the stipulation "ḥullanī ḥaythu ḥabastanī" affect the ruling?
ai.summary: This hadith gives a legal ruling related to iḥrām restriction in hajj or ʿumrah. It indicates that if a person is prevented by Allah from proceeding, the ruling of release applies at the point of hindrance whether or not he verbally stipulates it.

en.bab-ul-qaim-publications: Hadith.2561 - Humran ibn A'yan asked Imam (as) about a person who says,
"Release me where You have restrained me."
Imam (as) said: "He is released where Allah (swt), the Almighty, has restrained him, whether he says it or does not say it."
